Results: After matching, each group included 81 patients. Median TTF was 4.8 months in the <500-bed group and 4.9 months in the ≥500-bed group. In crude analyses, severe leukopenia occurred in 67.9% of patients in smaller hospitals and 45.7% in larger hospitals (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.51-0.89; p = 0.007), whereas severe neutropenia occurred in 79.0% and 58.0% of patients, respectively (RR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.59-0.91; p = 0.006). In sensitivity analyses accounting for hospital-level clustering, the association for leukopenia was maintained, whereas that for neutropenia was no longer statistically significant. Conclusions: No clear difference in TTF was observed between the hospital-size groups. Exploratory safety analyses showed differences in severe hematological toxicities, although the findings were not fully consistent after accounting for hospital-level clustering. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between institutional healthcare resources and treatment outcomes.

title: Etoposide-induced angina in a patient with small cell lung carcinoma: a case report.
authors: Otsuka S, Chiba Y, Otsuka K et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of cisplatin and etoposide is a standard therapy for small cell lung cancer; however, ischemic heart disease is a known complication. We report a rare case of effort angina pectoris that worsened during initial treatment of small cell lung cancer with etoposide.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old Asian male was admitted to our hospital with effort angina. Coronary angiography revealed severe stenosis with significant calcification of the proximal right coronary artery. Computed tomography revealed a 21-mm-sized nodule in the right upper lobe and hilar lymphadenopathy suggestive of lung cancer. The patient underwent thoracoscopic wedge resection before coronary revascularization, and intraoperative findings indicated a small cell carcinoma with hilar lymph node metastases. Early postoperative definitive treatment consisting of chemotherapy with cisplatin plus etoposide and accelerated hyperfractionated radiation was planned. During the first chemotherapy session, on postoperative day 7, the patient complained of chest pain, and an electrocardiogram showed slight ST depression in leads V5 and V6 while receiving etoposide; nitroglycerin improved his symptoms. Although treatment was resumed with the administration of nicorandil the next day, the same symptoms were observed during the infusion of etoposide. Accordingly, chemoradiation therapy was suspended and revascularization of the right coronary artery was performed. Etoposide and cisplatin were readministered 3 days after revascularization, without any chest symptoms.
CONCLUSION: Chemotherapy for malignant tumors carries the risk of progression to coronary artery disease. To prevent serious ischemic events, sufficient discussions between oncologists and cardiologists and careful observation of chest symptoms are needed.

title: RNA sequencing reveals molecular subtypes across adenocarcinoma, squamous, and small cell lung cancer.
authors: Arora S, Suresh L, Thirimanne NH et al.
abstract: This study combines RNA sequencing data from 1,824 tumors across major lung cancer types to examine how tumor gene expression patterns relate to histologic diagnoses. The resulting reference landscape identifies nine transcriptional clusters, including a neuroendocrine-like adenocarcinoma group and regions with mixed histology. The clusters also show associations with clinical features, genetic alterations, immune characteristics, and survival. An interactive Oncoscape resource allows researchers to explore the integrated data and compare patient tumors with patient-derived xenograft models.

title: Metabolomics in Thoracic Oncology from Biomarker Discovery to Therapeutic Targeting: A Narrative Review.
authors: Mahmoud MA, Sharma G, Sarkaria IS et al.
abstract: Thoracic malignancies show context-dependent metabolic plasticity that influences growth, immune evasion, and treatment response. This review examines how metabolomics, stable-isotope tracing, and metabolic flux analysis complement molecular profiling in lung, esophageal, pleural, and thymic cancers. We distinguish metabolite abundance from isotope enrichment and quantitative flux, and review analytical platforms, computational workflows, histology-specific programs, immunometabolism, biomarkers, and therapy. Lung squamous cell carcinoma often depends on glycolysis, lung adenocarcinoma shows substrate and spatial heterogeneity, and molecular subsets of small cell lung cancer have preclinical vulnerabilities in arginine metabolism and guanosine nucleotide synthesis. Hypoxia and metabolite exchange among malignant, stromal, and immune cells may shape therapeutic resistance. Biofluid and tissue studies support early detection and monitoring, but most circulating signatures and findings in rare thoracic tumors remain exploratory. Translation is limited by confounding, incomplete metabolite identification, small cohorts, and limited external validation. Trials of unselected metabolic inhibitors have largely failed. Two biomarker-selected strategies have advanced: arginine deprivation in non-epithelioid pleural mesothelioma, a population enriched for argininosuccinate synthetase 1 (ASS1) deficiency, and PRMT5 inhibition in tumors with MTAP deletion. These results suggest that success may depend on selecting patients by a demonstrated metabolic dependency rather than by the plausibility of the target. Progress requires harmonized multicenter workflows, paired tissue and biofluid sampling, rigorous validation, and integration with spatial, single-cell, multi-omic, and clinical data.

title: Clinical Artificial Intelligence in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: From Early Detection and Computational Pathology to Precision Oncology.
authors: Bertolaccini L, Chiari M, Degiovanni S et al.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being developed to analyze radiological, histopathological, molecular, and clinical data across the non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) pathway. This narrative review examines representative applications through August 2026, focusing on intended clinical use, validation, and the evidence required to influence care. Studies were selected purposively for clinical relevance and methodological importance. Imaging models support investigation of nodule detection, malignancy estimation, and future lung cancer risk, although predictive performance does not establish the benefit of changing screening or diagnostic pathways. In computational pathology, models classify tissue, quantify morphological features, and estimate selected molecular alterations. Foundation models extend these capabilities, but their evaluation requires attention to pretraining provenance and independence of downstream testing. Histology-based molecular prediction does not currently justify replacing validated molecular assays; prioritization of testing requires prospective workflow evaluation. Models evaluated in immunotherapy-treated cohorts can predict response or survival, but these associations do not establish differential benefit between treatments. The principal limitations include selected retrospective populations, incomplete assessment of calibration and clinically relevant thresholds, uncertain transportability, and limited evaluation of model-guided care. Evidence should therefore be interpreted at the level of the individual system and intended decision. Prospective evaluation, appropriate comparators, explicit failure procedures, and post-deployment monitoring are required before technical performance can be translated into clinical benefit.

title: Protocol for a mixed-methods evaluation of a village doctor-led implementation strategy for lung cancer screening in rural China: a positive deviance approach.
authors: Zhang Y, Shao M, Wang X et al.

title: Historical and projected smoking patterns and lung cancer incidence across sex and birth-cohorts in Spain: The rising burden in women.
authors: Cabrera MO, Borras JM, Espinàs JA et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Smoking prevalence varies greatly by sex across Europe. In Spain, while smoking prevalence has decreased in men, it has risen in women in the past decades and is now amongst the highest in Europe. However, there has been limited research into how changes in smoking prevalence impact long-term lung cancer incidence. This study analyses sex and birth-cohort specific smoking patterns in Spain and their impact on future lung cancer incidence.
METHODS: We used the MIcrosimulation SCreening Analysis (MISCAN)-Lung to evaluate and project smoking behaviour patterns and lung cancer incidence in Spain by sex and birth-cohort, using cancer registry data and nationally representative surveys from years 1987-2020.
FINDINGS: By 2035, current smoking prevalence in women born between 1955-1969 is expected to be higher than men (19.1 % current smoking prevalence for women compared to 14.1 % in men for the 1965-1969 birth-cohort). In men, lung cancer incidence per 100,000 person-years between 2015 and 2035 for those aged 55-64 and 65-79 is expected to decrease by 57.6 % (from 193.3 to 82.0 per 100,000) and 13.0 % (from 329.8 to 287.0 per 100,000), respectively. While a similar decline in incidence is projected for women aged 55-64 (from 74.5 to 29.8 per 100,000; 60.0 % decrease), incidence in ages 65-79 will increase by 171.6 % (from 48.6 to 132.0 per 100,000).
INTERPRETATION: Lung cancer incidence in women aged 65-79 in Spain is expected to increase considerably in the next decade. Given the variation in smoking prevalence by sex across Europe, the evaluation of sex differentiated prevention and early detection strategies for lung cancer are pivotal.

title: Risk of Developing a Subsequent Primary Lung Cancer Among Adult Non-Lung Cancer Survivors: Implications for Lung Cancer Screening and Supportive Care.
authors: Warkentin MT, Ruan Y, Harsanyi H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: An increasing number of people are living with and beyond a cancer diagnosis. We aim to characterize the risk of developing a subsequent primary lung cancer (SPLC) among survivors of non-lung first primary cancers (FPC).
METHODS: All adults diagnosed with cancer in Alberta between 2000 and 2021 who survived 6+ months were included. We estimated incidence rate differences and standardized incidence ratios (SIR) for SPLC compared to the cancer-free population and high-risk individuals included in a lung cancer screening trial. Multivariable Fine-Gray models were used to identify risk factors within cancer survivorship groups.
RESULTS: Cancer survivors (n = 180,325) have a higher risk of developing SPLC compared to those without a personal cancer history overall (SIR = 1.37, 95% Confidence Interval: 1.32-1.42) and at later stages (III/IV). The increase in late-stage SPLC risk was highest beyond 5 years from FPC diagnosis. About 13 out of 21 FPC sites have significant increases in SPLC risk and smoking-related FPC sites carried the highest risks. For survivors of head and neck or bladder cancers, the 6-year absolute risks of developing SPLC were 2.7% and 2.6%, respectively, which is higher than the thresholds commonly used for lung screening program eligibility. Five FPC sites had SIRs higher than the control arm of a lung cancer screening trial. Site-specific SPLC risk varied by age, sex, socioeconomic status, comorbidities, stage of FPC, and treatments.
CONCLUSION: Cancer survivors carry significant risks of developing SPLC yet many survivors may not be considered for long term surveillance or screening for early lung cancer detection.

title: De Novo Lung Cancer after Lung Transplantation: Rethinking Surveillance and Early Detection.
authors: Mehdizadeh-Shrifi A, Lennartz F, Merhej H et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: While lung transplantation (LTx) is an established therapy for end-stage lung disease in an aging population, lung cancer (LC) complicates the transplant journey. This study aimed to elucidate factors associated with LC development and post-diagnosis mortality.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center observational study at a certified lung cancer center of patients with primary LC after LTx between 1997 and 2025. Characteristics, survival and predictors of development of LC and mortality were assessed.
RESULTS: Of 2,541 LTx recipients, 47 developed LC, corresponding to an incidence of 1.9%. The median time from LTx to LC diagnosis was 6.05 [3.44-8.89] years. Age at transplantation was 55 [IQR 45-59] years; donor age was 52 [46-60] years. Most tumors arose in the transplanted lung (N = 33, 70%). Survival following LC diagnosis was 0.57 [0.22-1.64] years. Unilateral LTx (HR 2.89), donor smoking history (HR 1.82), ILD/pulmonary fibrosis (HR 1.49), older recipient age (HR 1.37 per 10 years), and cumulative recipient smoking exposure (HR 1.13 per 10 pack-years) were associated with LC development. Stage-IV disease (HR 2.56), unilateral LTx (HR 2.13), prolonged time to LC diagnosis (HR 2.09), and advanced donor age (HR 2.03) were associated with mortality.
CONCLUSION: Lung cancer after LTx is a rare complication with poor prognosis. Recipient-, donor, and transplant-related characteristics were associated with LC development, while advanced-stage disease and selected transplant-related factors were associated with mortality. Screening protocols should be intensified in an aging LTx population.

title: Clinical Utility of Next Generation Sequencing in Concurrent EBUS-TBNA and Liquid Biopsies in NSCLC.

title: Advances in Biomarker Discovery for Early Ovarian Cancer Diagnosis.
authors: Niebora J, Spaczyńska J, Partyńska A et al.
abstract: Ovarian cancer is one of the deadliest gynecological cancers worldwide. One promising therapeutic approach is the use of combined biomarkers. The Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) which combines CA125 with Human Epididymal Protein 4 (HE4) is an example of combining biomarkers to gain an optimal predictive outcome. Tumor Protein p53 (TP53) is a transcription factor with tumor suppressor properties. Mutations in TP53 constitute the most frequent genetic alterations observed in ovarian cancer. In contrast to conventional markers such as CA125, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) provides information about tumor mutations and insights into treatment response. Analysis of ctDNA enables the identification of tumor-associated mutations. Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) also influence cellular processes and act as effectors in oncogenic pathways by binding to RNA or proteins. One effector is Metastasis-Associated Lung Adenocarcinoma Transcript 1 (MALAT1), whose increased expression is associated with an aggressive tumor phenotype. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are crucial in regulating the expression of genes associated with ovarian cancer development and progression. Exosomes carrying various molecules, including miRNAs and lncRNAs, contribute to ovarian cancer progression. Adipocytokines play an important role in the regulation of metabolic and inflammatory processes. Despite their diagnostic potential, the identified biomarkers require further validation.

title: Real-World Clinical Outcomes and Treatment Patterns in Patients with Unresectable Stage III NSCLC Treated with CCRT With or Without Durvalumab as Consolidation Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Rai P, Kao YH, Hu X et al.
abstract: Background: Durvalumab is currently approved as consolidation therapy for patients with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without disease progression following concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT). This study described real-world characteristics, disease progression, subsequent treatment, and clinical outcomes according to durvalumab receipt. Methods: This retrospective cohort study used the N-Power Medicine database. Adults diagnosed with unresectable stage III NSCLC who initiated cCRT between February 2018 and October 2023 and subsequently received durvalumab or no durvalumab and were followed until October 2025. Baseline characteristics, disease progression, and subsequent treatment patterns were summarized descriptively. Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate overall survival (OS) and time to death or distant metastasis (TDDM). Results: Among 717 patients who initiated cCRT, 487 received cCRT followed by durvalumab and 230 received cCRT only. Baseline characteristics were broadly similar between cohorts. Median theoretical follow-up was 60.5 and 60.8 months, respectively. Disease progression was observed in both groups, with higher rates in the cCRT-only cohort (48.7% vs. 40.9%). TDDM was 26.7 months in the cCRT + durvalumab cohort and 5.6 months in the cCRT-only cohort. Median OS was 42.6 months and 11.4 months, and OS events occurred in 55.2% and 80.0% of patients, respectively. In the cCRT + durvalumab cohort, OS rates at 12, 36 and 60 months were 83.6%, 56.0%, and 42.8%. Conclusions: In real-world practice, approximately one-third of patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC did not receive durvalumab following cCRT. Despite consolidation therapy, a substantial proportion of patients continue to experience disease progression, highlighting ongoing unmet need in this population.

title: Indocyanine Green and Technetium-99m: CT-Guided Marking of Lung Nodules Before Robotic-Assisted Lung Resection.
authors: Ferrante F, Ricciardi S, Ventroni G et al.
abstract: Background/Objectives: For stage I non-small cell lung cancer, surgery remains the cornerstone of treatment and the use of minimally invasive techniques is desirable. The lack of tactile feedback in RATS is a well-known drawback of this approach, so precise identification of the disease is crucial for performing lung resection. Methods: We present our retrospective case history, accounting for 83 patients, which were divided into two groups based on marking technique: 99mTc-MAA (99mTechnetium Albumin Macroaggregates) only (Tech group) (22 cases, 26.5%) and 99mTc-MAA + Indocyanine Green (Tech + ICG group) (61 cases, 73.49%). Results: In the Tech group, there were 11 males (50%) ad 11 females (50%), the median nodule diameter was 21.5 mm (IQR 16), and the median distance of the nodule from the visceral pleura was 18 mm (IQR 21). Eighteen out of 22 nodules (81.82%) were subsolid. Three conversions were reported, all due to failure to identify the nodule (13.63%). The mean operative time was 111.6 ± 45.6 min. The histopathological examination resulted in 13 lung adenocarcinomas, one squamous cell carcinoma, two minimally invasive lung adenocarcinomas, two lung adenocarcinomas in situ, three metastases from another tumor, and one benign nodule. In the Tech + ICG group, there were 27 males (44.26%) and 34 females (55.73%), the median nodule diameter was 18 mm (IQR 14), and the median distance of the nodule from the visceral pleura was 24 mm (IQR 15). Forty-six out of 61 nodules were subsolid (75.4%). Four conversions were reported, due to failure in nodule identification (6.55%). The operative time was 105.6 ± 36.8 min. The histopathological examination resulted in 12 lung adenocarcinomas, seven squamous cell carcinomas, nine minimally invasive lung adenocarcinomas, 12 lung adenocarcinomas in situ, one typical carcinoid, seven atypical adenomatous hyperplasias, seven metastases from another tumor, and six benign nodules. The two groups are homogeneous in terms of median nodule diameter (p = 0.676), the median distance from visceral pleura (p = 0.114), SUV max (p = 0.894), operative time (p = 0.512), and nodule characteristics (solid vs. subsolid) (p = 0.724). The conversion rate was lower in the Tech + ICG group (6.55% vs. 13.63%), but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.375). Conclusions: Both techniques appear to be safe and reproducible. Further standardized studies are needed to validate and confirm the results obtained from our case series.

title: Measured Postoperative DL,CO and FEV1 Frequently Exceed Segment-Count Predictions After Lung Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Hartmeyer HL, Bang CK, Alstrup G et al.
abstract: Background: The segment count method (SCM) is standard for predicting post-operative pulmonary function tests (ppo-PFTs) in patients undergoing surgical resection for non-small cell lung cancer. Accurate prediction is pivotal for providing optimal treatment; however, earlier studies indicate that SCM underestimates ppo-PFTs. This study aimed to investigate whether this underestimation correlates with the specific lobe resected or pre-operative PFT values. Methods: This retrospective single-centre study evaluated patients who underwent surgical resection (wedge, segmentectomy, or lobectomy) for lung cancer. Clinical data were extracted from electronic medical files. PFTs (forced expiratory volume in the first second, FEV1, and diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide, DL,CO) were performed before and within 1 year after surgery and reported as % predicted. The SCMs were calculated as the pre-operative PFTs minus the proportion related to the number of resected segments. Pre-operative DL,CO was categorised as 40-60%, 61-80%, and >80%. Results: In total, 117 patients were included (lobectomy n = 102, wedge resection n = 15). PFTs were preserved with wedge resection. In patients undergoing lobectomy, a >10% prediction error of SCM on DL,CO was observed in 74% (FEV1: 63%) and most often due to higher-than-predicted (DL,CO: 63%; FEV1: 52%) than lower-than-predicted PFT (DL,CO: 11%; FEV1: 11%). A higher BMI was significantly associated with lower-than-predicted PFTs. No association was found regarding the resected lobe. Notably, the prediction error of SCM increased with decreasing DL,CO: post-operative DL,CO was preserved in patients with pre-operative DL,CO 40-60%. Conclusions: The segment count method exhibits systematic imprecision that correlates inversely with baseline DL,CO levels. Further studies are needed to validate this finding and to investigate how the SCM can be refined to reduce prediction error, especially in patients with the lowest preoperative PFTs.

title: Survival predictors in unresectable stage III NSCLC treated with induction chemoimmunotherapy: a real-world multicenter study of treatment cycles, response, and maintenance duration.
authors: Shi Y, Hu X, Liu C et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal integration of induction chemoimmunotherapy with definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and maintenance immunotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC remains undefined.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 321 patients who received induction chemoimmunotherapy followed by CRT with or without maintenance immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Landmark survival from radiotherapy completion was used to avoid guarantee-time bias.
RESULTS: Patients receiving 1-2 induction cycles showed numerically longer median PFS (28.0 months) than those with 3-4 (24.6) or >4 cycles (14.2; log-rank p = 0.179), but this trend was confounded by higher concurrent CRT rates in the 1-2 cycle group (74.5%vs. 47.1% vs. 33.7%). After propensity-score matching, the response-related survival advantage was attenuated (HR for PFS 0.70, p = 0.079). In matched analyses, maintenance ICI was associated with improved PFS (25.2 vs. 8.9 months; HR 0.47) and OS (NR vs. 22.0 months; HR 0.24) (both p < 0.001). An exploratory data-driven analysis suggested that >9 maintenance cycles yielded further PFS (HR 0.23) and OS (HR 0.17) benefits.
CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, induction cycle number did not significantly affect survival; the apparent advantage of 1-2 cycles was likely confounded. Early radiographic response was not an independent predictor after matching. Maintenance ICI was associated with improved outcomes, and >9 cycles showed additional benefit, though with potential bias. These findings provide hypotheses for prospective trial design.

title: Comparison of whole-lung, physical-dose, and BED3-guided subregional multi-omics for predicting 3-month symptomatic radiation pneumonitis after lung cancer radiotherapy: a dual-center study.
authors: Liu L, Wang S, Li X et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Region definition may influence radiation pneumonitis (RP) prediction, particularly when treatment schedules differ. We compared whole-lung, physical-dose subregional, and voxelwise biologically effective dose with α/β = 3 Gy (BED3)-guided strategies. The target outcome was grade ≥ 2 symptomatic RP within 3 months after lung cancer radiotherapy.
METHODS: This retrospective dual-center study included 246 patients between March 2023 and December 2025: 171 in a hospital-defined development cohort and 75 in the center-2 assessment cohort. The outcome was any grade ≥ 2 symptomatic RP recorded within 3 months after radiotherapy. Seven clinical, DVH, radiomic, dosiomic, and combined model specifications were evaluated within each region-design strategy. Development used repeated stratified 5 × 5 nested cross-validation and optimism correction based on 1000 bootstrap samples. All candidate models used the same outer and corresponding inner partitions and bootstrap resamples. Center 2 was excluded from model development and optimism correction and was used for center-specific out-of-sample performance assessment.
RESULTS: Forty-three patients developed grade ≥ 2 symptomatic RP (27/171 in development; 16/75 in center 2). Under shared resampling, center-2 AUCs for the complete whole-lung, physical-dose, and BED3 models were 0.676, 0.669, and 0.684, respectively. The differences were small, with overlapping confidence intervals. Across five intervals per representation, the highest point estimates were observed for physical dose 10-20 Gy (AUC 0.745) and BED3 ≥ 70 Gy3 (AUC 0.720). These interval rankings are exploratory and subject to selection optimism. Center-2 Brier scores for the complete models ranged from 0.184 to 0.260, compared with 0.168 for a constant-probability reference based on the center-2 event rate; calibration was inadequate for clinical use.
CONCLUSIONS: The paired analysis did not identify a clearly superior region design. Complete-model center-2 AUCs differed by at most 0.015, with overlapping confidence intervals. Physical dose 10-20 Gy and BED3 ≥ 70 Gy3 produced the highest interval-level point estimates, but these rankings are exploratory. Recalibration and prospective multicenter validation are required before clinical use.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

title: The "Heat-and-Cold" Strategy: Combining Intercostal Nerve Cryoablation for Analgesia After Uniportal VATS Pleurectomy and Hyperthermic Intrathoracic Chemotherapy.
authors: Nachira D, Punzo G, Calabrese G et al.
abstract: We report interesting images from a 54-year-old woman with recurrent B2 thymoma associated with myasthenia gravis, treated using a minimally invasive uniportal VATS pleurectomy combined with hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy (HITHOC). Preoperative imaging identified two hypermetabolic pleural lesions. Complete resection was achieved, followed by cisplatin-based HITHOC. Postoperative pain was managed by a multimodal approach combining erector spinae plane block and intercostal nerve cryoablation, resulting in a VAS score of two on the first postoperative day, decreasing to zero subsequently, and with no opioid requirement to control pain. The patient experienced an uneventful recovery and rapid discharge. This case highlights the feasibility and safety, with favourable outcomes in this patient. Larger and comparative series are needed to confirm the potential advantages of combining minimally invasive surgery with advanced analgesic strategies in complex thoracic oncology.

title: Does Thymoma Plus Hypogammaglobulinemia Define Good Syndrome? A 30-Year Longitudinal Study of a Single Patient with Persistent B-Cell Preservation.
authors: Iguasnia Portilla D, Castillo Castillo I, Franco Figueroa V et al.
abstract: Good syndrome is commonly diagnosed when thymoma and hypogammaglobulinemia coexist, although universally accepted diagnostic criteria are lacking. Profound B-cell lymphopenia is one of its most consistent immunological features. We describe a woman followed for 30 years in our unit whose severe antibody deficiency preceded thymoma detection by 14 years. Circulating B cells were preserved before thymectomy and throughout 16 years of subsequent follow-up, with maintained class-switched memory B cells despite persistent antibody deficiency. Her clinical course was favorable under immunoglobulin replacement, without documented major opportunistic infections. T-cell differentiation abnormalities were present despite preserved absolute counts. These findings suggest that patients currently classified as Good syndrome may represent a more heterogeneous group than traditionally assumed. Although preserved B cells do not exclude Good syndrome under existing definitions, the present observation should be considered hypothesis-generating and supports further studies evaluating potential biological heterogeneity among patients diagnosed with Good syndrome. This case highlights the need for consensus diagnostic criteria that consider the temporal relationship between both conditions, B-cell numbers, and the accompanying immune abnormalities, rather than relying on the coexistence of thymoma and hypogammaglobulinemia alone.

title: Beyond Mesothelioma: From Diagnostic Biomarker to Therapeutic Opportunity-The Emerging Role of MTAP in Cancer.
authors: Diluvio A, Lucà S, Iavarone L et al.
abstract: Methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP) loss is an emerging biomarker in several human malignancies, mainly due to its frequent co-deletion with CDKN2A on chromosome 9p21. Beyond its diagnostic value, MTAP deficiency has important biological consequences, including metabolic reprogramming, immune microenvironment modulation, and increased dependency on PRMT5-related pathways. This review summarizes the current evidence on MTAP alterations across different tumor types. The role of MTAP immunohistochemistry as a practical surrogate for CDKN2A homozygous deletion is discussed, together with its advantages and interpretative limitations. In addition, the potential predictive relevance of MTAP loss for immunotherapy, antifolate-based treatments, and novel PRMT5-targeted strategies is explored. Overall, MTAP assessment represents a promising tool in modern diagnostic pathology and precision oncology, bridging morphology, molecular alterations, and therapeutic decision-making.

title: Hassall's Corpuscles as Dynamic and Functionally Specialized Structures.
authors: Odaka C, Hub E, Rot A
abstract: Hassall's corpuscles were first described in 1846 by the British physician and anatomist Arthur Hill Hassall. During histological observations of the human thymus, he discovered distinctive concentric epithelial structures within the medulla, which he termed "Hassall's corpuscles". Hassall's corpuscles are also called Hassall's bodies. These structures share morphological and molecular features with the epidermis. Since Hassall's corpuscles express late keratinization markers such as involucrin, keratin 10, and filaggrin, they are considered to be composed of terminally differentiated medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs). Recent fate-mapping and single-cell transcriptomic analyses have demonstrated that Hassall's corpuscles originate from post-Aire mTECs, and their differentiation has been suggested to be Aire-dependent. Hassall's corpuscles are now recognized as heterogeneous structures that play a role in central tolerance and regulatory T cell (Treg) development. In this review, we summarize recent advances in our understanding of the development of Hassall's corpuscles within the mTEC lineage. We further describe that Hassall's corpuscles undergo dynamic changes in size and number during thymic involution and regeneration. Thus, we propose that Hassall's corpuscles should no longer be regarded as merely regressive structures but rather as functionally active bodies with critical immunological roles.

title: Real-World Outcomes of Oral VEGFR Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Containing Therapy in Unresectable Malignant Mesothelioma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
authors: Liu Z, Zhong J, Wan R et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic treatment choices after failure of standard therapy are limited for malignant mesothelioma. Oral vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (VEGFR-TKIs) have been incorporated into salvage treatment strategies, but real-world evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety remains scarce.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a single-center cohort comprising patients with pathologically confirmed malignant mesothelioma treated at Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences/National Cancer Center between 1 April 2017 and 16 March 2023. Patients with unresectable disease who received a VEGFR-TKI-containing regimen and had sufficient clinical follow-up for outcome assessment were included. Progression-free survival (PFS) served as the primary endpoint. Objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS) from VEGFR-TKI initiation, and recorded adverse events were included as secondary endpoints.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 48 patients, with a median follow-up of 24.0 months. The Kaplan-Meier estimated median PFS was 4.8 months (95% CI, 2.9-8.8), and median OS from VEGFR-TKI initiation was 17.9 months (95% CI, 13.5-not estimable). Among 39 response-evaluable patients, 6 achieved partial response, 20 had stable disease, and 13 had progressive disease as their best overall response, yielding an ORR of 15.4% and a DCR of 66.7%. Two patients remained progression-free for more than 24 months. Grade 3 adverse events in the records included hematuria, hypertension, and nausea/vomiting; no grade 4 or grade 5 adverse event was documented.
CONCLUSIONS: VEGFR-TKI-containing therapy was associated with clinically relevant disease control in unresectable malignant mesothelioma, with durable benefit observed in a small subset of patients. These observations warrant further evaluation of VEGFR-TKI-based salvage strategies in larger multicenter cohorts.

title: BRCA1-Associated Protein 1 in Sarcoma.
authors: Liu X, Haugh W, Zhang Z et al.
abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) are genetically complex mesenchymal tumors with limited therapeutic options. BRCA1-associated protein 1 (BAP1), a deubiquitinase, is a critical regulator of chromatin architecture, DNA repair, and cell cycle control. While BAP1 alterations are well-characterized in mesothelioma and uveal melanoma, their role in STS remains understudied. Increasing evidence shows BAP1 alterations are associated with STS. This review summarizes current evidence on BAP1 biology and its emerging significance in sarcoma. We discuss BAP1's molecular functions, including its role in the Polycomb Repressive Deubiquitinase (PR-DUB) complex, and summarize recent findings implicating BAP1 loss in multiple subtypes of STS. We highlight mechanistic links between BAP1 deficiency, genomic instability, and tumor progression, and explore therapeutic implications such as polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1) inhibition and epigenetic modulation. Understanding BAP1-driven pathways in STS may uncover novel biomarkers and targeted strategies, addressing a critical unmet need in sarcoma management.

title: Review of Registries, Databases and Biobanks for Surveillance and Research on Mesothelioma.
authors: Prabhakaran S, Driscoll T, Barker S et al.
abstract: Mesothelioma is considered a signal tumour of asbestos exposure. Many countries have imposed asbestos bans or effectively no longer use asbestos, but a small number continue to import or mine it. Controls are generally much improved, with resulting plateauing or decreasing rates in many countries, but the effect of past exposures and ongoing exposure through in situ asbestos in buildings and environmental sources results in continued cases of mesothelioma globally. Improper disposal of asbestos is also an obstacle to managing and reducing asbestos exposure. Data on mesothelioma are recorded by mesothelioma registries, population-based cancer registries, healthcare databases, biobanks and online epidemiological data sources. Data from the various sources are significantly different and generally not directly comparable. Mesothelioma registries and population-based cancer registries are excellent resources for epidemiological and statistical data but are typically not linked to clinical data or biospecimen collections. Integrating biospecimen collections with linked clinical data creates rich real-world datasets that enhance research quality, enable data-driven discoveries, and support future translational research. The diagnosis of mesothelioma can be challenging, and data recording is not always accurate or complete across centres. Inconsistencies in data can affect epidemiological studies and undermine efforts to improve policies that affect individuals with mesothelioma and prevent further occurrence of mesothelioma. Linkage between mesothelioma registries, cancer registries, biobanks and other health-related databases will benefit researchers and allow access for further research initiatives. Closer collaboration between registries offers benefits for countries that lack diagnostic and healthcare infrastructure. Established mesothelioma registries can serve as valuable models for countries developing national surveillance systems by sharing expertise in case ascertainment, exposure assessment, registry governance and epidemiological methods. This study is a narrative review based on a non-systematic search of the published literature. This review of mesothelioma-related data resources and biospecimen collections serves as a foundation for enhancing collaboration and knowledge sharing in the fight against mesothelioma.

title: Final analysis from PECATI phase 2 trial, lenvatinib in combination with pembrolizumab in pretreated advanced B3-thymoma and thymic carcinoma.
authors: Remon J, Bironzo P, Girard N et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is no standard second-line treatment for patients with platinum-refractory advanced B3-Thymoma (T) and thymic carcinoma (TC). In this population, the PECATI trial (NCT04710628) testing the combination lenvatinib and pembrolizumab met its primary endpoint, with 5-month progression-free survival (PFS) of 88.0%. Here we report the final clinical study results.
METHODS: PECATI is a single-arm, phase 2 trial enrolling patients with metastatic B3-T and TC, without autoimmune disorders that have progressed following at least one platinum-based chemotherapy. The trial evaluated lenvatinib (20 mg orally once daily) plus pembrolizumab (200 mg iv infusion once every 3 weeks) in 3-week cycles for a maximum of 35 cycles if no disease progression or toxicity.
RESULTS: 43 patients were enrolled: median age 57 years (33-81); 84% had a TC; 65% Masaoka Koga IVB, 51.2% of patients with ≥3 metastatic sites, and 44.2% received ≥2 prior lines for advanced disease. After a median follow-up of 24.6 months, the median PFS was 22.1 months (95%CI: 10.9-25.1), and the median overall survival (OS) was 40.2 months (95%CI: 19.1-not estimated), with 36-month OS rate of 53.0%. The confirmed ORR was 25.6% and median duration of response was not reached. The rate of grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events was 44.2% leading to treatment discontinuation in 27.9% of cases. Two (4.7%) non-treatment-related grade 5 events were reported. The rate of grade 3 immune-related adverse events was 11.6%.
CONCLUSION: The final results of PECATI trial supports the combination lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab as a potential treatment option in pre-treated advanced B3-thymoma and thymic carcinoma. Toxicity profile is manageable but close monitoring is advised.
